messages:
jia: Quick heads-up — onboarding MistralCascade-v1 (int4) to Dedicated pool. Longctx smoke (4k tokens) shows token dropout starting ~2k, outputs become repetitive/blank. Repro script: `/tmp/cascade_repro.py` on the canary cluster.

eli: Can you paste the tokenizer sample around the boundary? sounds like vocab offset/aliasing. Also which conversion tool did you use for quant?

jia: Using `redwood-model-convert v0.9` -> `mistral->redwood` + int4 quant from our inttool. Example token window where it dies: ```
>> tokens[2036:2048] = [1204, 502, 13, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0]
>> output[:,2036:2048] = [[0.01, -0.02, ... 0.0]]
```

sam: That token pattern (zeros) smells like a KV-cache address wrap or a rotary/headstride mismatch. Mistral grads use headwise proj order in some checkpoints; Llama style is different. If the projorder got flipped during conversion, rotary embeddings can destructively cancel after long contexts.

marta: Quick eval: fp16 baseline on same sequences gives ppl=12.1, int4 converted model ppl=13.8 on short ctx. On longctx the int4 drops to weird outputs — rouge scores on summarization drop ~-4.1 compared to fp16. So it's probably not purely quant noise.

eli: Can you dump the KV keys/rotary angles for a failing run? e.g. `python -m infratools.dump_kv --model mistralcascade-v1 --range 2000-2060` and attach. Also check tokenizer normalization: `nlp_tokenizer.normalize(text, form='NFKC')` — weird whitespace/zero-width may shift ids.

jia: Dump attached in the canary logs: `kv_keys_t2036 = [0x3f12aa, 0x3f12ab, 0x0, 0x0, ...]` — see zeros aligning with token zeros. Conversion diff I found: original weight layout: `q,k,v -> qkv` while our convert wrote `k,q,v` for some attention blocks. Patch diff: ```- q,k,v
+ k,q,v```

sam: Yup that's the projorder flip. Two followups: 1) rotary phase uses head index mapping; if projorder flips the projected vectors fed into rotary, phase pairs misalign and cancel out eventually. 2) int4 kernel packing may assume contiguous head layout; if we changed headstride during conversion, pack/unpack mismatch occurs.

eli: Proposed quick fix: add a conversion flag `--force-projorder=qkv` to the convert tool and re-run quant. Command: `redwood-model-convert --src mistral --dst redwood --force-projorder=qkv --out /tmp/mc_v1_fixed`

ci-bot: Test run kicked off: `longctx-smoke (canary)` for build 1715504321-fix1. Logs: "STEP: canary deploy -> smoke run" 
ci-bot: Result: `FAIL` — regression persists. Metrics: longctx-rouge = -3.2 vs fp16, leaks after token 2040.

marta: I ran a quick manual experiment: toggling `rotary_scale` between `0.5` and `1.0` changes where the collapse happens (0.5 -> collapse earlier, 1.0 -> later but still). So scale matters but doesn't eliminate it. Suggest we bisect the conversion kernels (headstride, projorder, pack order).

sam: I'll run a kernel-bisect in parallel: toggle `headstride = native|packed` and `projorder = qkv|kqv` and dump outputs. If swapping projorder fixes it, we need a permanent conversion guard. If not, kernel pack likely wrong.

jia: For immediate mitigation, I'm going to set canary routing policy to fall back to the fp16 variant for longctx routes: `route.longctx.model = fp16-mistralcascade-v1`. Rolling canary now, please monitor.

marta: Running full eval pipeline on the patched conversion + projorder forced. ETA 25m, will post numbers. If that passes, we should add a tokenizer/tag check to conversion CI (catch if projorder mismatch).

eli: Thanks — one more ask: after we confirm, add a tiny unit test: feed a 3k token sequence that intentionally crosses head boundary and assert output token distribution entropy doesn't drop by >20% after 2k. Saves future regressions.

jia: Agreed. I'll file a follow-up PR with conversion guard + CI test. Filing: https://github.com/redwood-inference/model-convert/pull/298 (draft).
